solution.explanation: Cells that do not divide further exit G1 and enter G0. Cells in this stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so, depending on the requirement of the organism. So A is true and R is false.
steps: R: false, G0 cells do not proliferate unless called on to do so
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (Phases of Cell Cycle)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about a cell at metaphase II of meiosis in a diploid (2n) organism are correct?

(a) The cell has n chromosomes.
(b) Each chromosome has two chromatids.
(c) The homologous chromosomes are paired as bivalents.
(d) Microtubules from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores of the sister chromatids.
(e) The cell has 4C DNA.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes, so each cell entering meiosis II has n chromosomes, each still made of two sister chromatids (2C DNA, half of the 4C of the meiocyte after S phase). At metaphase II the chromosomes align at the equator and microtubules from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids. Bivalents exist only in prophase I and metaphase I.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (c) or (e), or leaves out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Meiosis II)
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the oocytes of some vertebrates, diplotene can last for months or years.
Reason (R): Diakinesis is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements are true. A concerns the duration of diplotene in vertebrate oocytes. R describes the next stage, diakinesis, in which chiasmata terminalise. The terminalisation of chiasmata in a later stage does not explain why diplotene is prolonged, so R is not the explanation of A.
steps: R describes a different stage; it does not explain A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Prophase I)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following takes place in anaphase I of meiosis, but in neither the anaphase of mitosis nor anaphase II of meiosis?

options.text: Separation of homologous chromosomes, while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres
Movement of chromosomes towards the opposite poles
Shortening of the microtubules attached to the kinetochores

solution.explanation: In anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate, while the sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres. In the anaphase of mitosis and in anaphase II the centromeres split and sister chromatids separate. Movement towards the poles occurs in all three anaphases.
steps: Anaphase I: homologues separate, centromeres intact
Mitotic anaphase and anaphase II: centromeres split, chromatids separate
solution.why_others_wrong: Splitting of the centromere occurs in mitotic anaphase and anaphase II, not anaphase I. Poleward movement and the shortening of kinetochore microtubules are not unique to anaphase I.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Anaphase); Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Separation of homologous chromosomes, while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cell growth, in terms of cytoplasmic increase, continues through the cell cycle, but DNA is synthesised in only one specific stage.
Statement II: In animal cells, DNA replication begins in the nucleus during the S phase, while the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Growth and DNA synthesis in the cell cycle
solution.explanation: NCERT states that although cell growth (in terms of cytoplasmic increase) is a continuous process, DNA synthesis occurs only during one specific stage, the S phase. In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (Phases of Cell Cycle)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A graph that shows the rate of photosynthesis at different wavelengths of light is called the:

solution.explanation: A graph of the absorption of light of different wavelengths by a pigment is its absorption spectrum. A graph of the rate of photosynthesis against wavelength is the action spectrum. NCERT superimposes the two to show that most photosynthesis takes place in the blue and red regions, where chlorophyll a absorbs most.
steps: Rate of photosynthesis vs wavelength → action spectrum
solution.why_others_wrong: The absorption spectrum plots light absorbed by a pigment, not the rate of photosynthesis. The Z scheme shows electron carriers on a redox scale. A chromatogram separates pigments.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', What is our Understanding of the Pigments Involved in Photosynthesis?
solution.final_answer: Option C: action spectrum

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following leaf pigments is NOT an accessory pigment?

solution.explanation: Chlorophyll a is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis and forms the reaction centre. Chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids are called accessory pigments: they also absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a.
solution.why_others_wrong: Chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids are the accessory pigments named by NCERT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', What is our Understanding of the Pigments Involved in Photosynthesis?
solution.final_answer: Option D: Chlorophyll a

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the leaves of a plant, large bundle sheath cells with many chloroplasts, thick walls and no intercellular spaces form a wreath around the vascular bundles. Which of the following plants shows this anatomy?

solution.explanation: This is Kranz ('wreath') anatomy, a characteristic of C4 plants such as maize and sorghum. The bundle sheath cells have a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and no intercellular spaces. Tomato and bell pepper are named by NCERT as C3 plants grown in CO₂-enriched greenhouses.
steps: Wreath of bundle sheath cells → Kranz anatomy → C4 plant (maize)
solution.why_others_wrong: Tomato and bell pepper are C3 plants. Chlamydomonas is a unicellular green alga with no leaves or vascular bundles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option A: Maize

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In photosynthesis, green plants use light energy to drive the synthesis of organic compounds.
Statement II: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from the splitting of water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Photosynthesis is a physico-chemical process by which green plants use light energy to drive the synthesis of organic compounds. In the light reaction, water is split into H⁺, [O] and electrons on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane, and the oxygen evolved comes from this splitting of water.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Introduction; The Electron Transport (Splitting of Water)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The light-harvesting complexes (LHC) of Photosystem I and Photosystem II are located in the:

options.text: outer membrane of the chloroplast envelope

solution.explanation: Within the chloroplast, the membrane system (grana and stroma lamellae) is responsible for trapping light energy. The pigments are organised into two discrete light-harvesting complexes within PS I and PS II, located in the thylakoid membranes. The stroma carries out the enzymatic reactions that synthesise sugar.
solution.why_others_wrong: The stroma is the site of the biosynthetic phase. The chloroplast envelope and the mitochondrial membrane do not contain the photosystems.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where does Photosynthesis Take Place?; What is Light Reaction?
solution.final_answer: Option B: thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Oxygen is evolved in non-cyclic photophosphorylation but not in cyclic photophosphorylation.
Reason (R): The water splitting complex is associated with PS II, which does not take part in cyclic photophosphorylation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why cyclic photophosphorylation releases no oxygen
solution.explanation: Water is split by the water splitting complex associated with PS II, and this is the source of the oxygen evolved. In non-cyclic photophosphorylation PS II and PS I work in series, so water is split and O₂ released. In cyclic photophosphorylation only PS I is functional and the electron is circulated within it, so no water is split and no O₂ is evolved. R directly explains A.
steps: R: true; no PS II in the cyclic flow → no water splitting → no O₂
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Splitting of Water; Cyclic and Non-cyclic Photo-phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are listed by NCERT as special features of C4 plants?

(a) A special type of leaf anatomy
(b) Tolerance of higher temperatures
(c) A response to high light intensities
(d) Lack of photorespiration
(e) A lower productivity of biomass than C3 plants

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT states that C4 plants are special: they have a special type of leaf anatomy (Kranz anatomy), they tolerate higher temperatures, they show a response to high light intensities, they lack a process called photorespiration, and they have greater productivity of biomass.
steps: (e): false, C4 plants have greater productivity of biomass
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (e) or leaves out one of the true features.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are consumed in the Calvin cycle?

(a) CO₂
(b) ATP
(c) NADPH
(d) O₂
(e) Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The Calvin cycle fixes CO₂ (carboxylation), uses ATP for phosphorylation and NADPH for reduction (reduction stage), and uses ATP to regenerate RuBP. O₂ is a product of the light reaction, not an input of the Calvin cycle, and PEP is the CO₂ acceptor of the C4 pathway in mesophyll cells.
steps: O₂: product of light reaction; PEP: C4 pathway
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes O₂ or PEP, or leaves out one of the inputs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Calvin Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Photorespiration results in the synthesis of sugars and ATP.
Reason (R): In photorespiration, RuBP combines with O₂ to form one molecule of PGA and one of phosphoglycolate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In the photorespiratory pathway, RuBP binds O₂ instead of CO₂ and forms one molecule of PGA and phosphoglycolate. There is neither synthesis of sugars nor of ATP and NADPH; rather, CO₂ is released with the utilisation of ATP. So A is false and R is true.
steps: A: false, no sugar or ATP is synthesised
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Photorespiration
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (quantity in the Calvin cycle) with List-II (number).

List-I:
A. ATP used for every CO₂ fixed
B. NADPH used for every CO₂ fixed
C. Turns of the cycle needed to make one glucose
D. ATP used to make one glucose

List-II:
I. 18
II. 2
III. 6
IV. 3

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Energy accounting of the Calvin cycle
solution.explanation: For every CO₂ molecule entering the Calvin cycle, 3 molecules of ATP and 2 of NADPH are required. Six turns of the cycle are needed to make one molecule of glucose, so one glucose uses 6 × 3 = 18 ATP and 6 × 2 = 12 NADPH.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap ATP and NADPH per CO₂, swap turns and total ATP, or confuse ATP per CO₂ with the number of turns.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Calvin Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly shows the path of electrons in non-cyclic photophosphorylation?

options.text: H₂O → PS II → electron transport chain (cytochromes) → PS I → NADP⁺
H₂O → PS I → electron transport chain → PS II → NADP⁺
NADP⁺ → PS I → electron transport chain → PS II → H₂O
H₂O → PS II → NADP⁺ → PS I → electron transport chain

solution.explanation: Electrons lost by PS II are replaced by electrons from the splitting of water. Electrons excited in PS II pass through an electron transport system of cytochromes to PS I, not being used up on the way. Electrons excited in PS I are passed through another chain to NADP⁺, reducing it to NADPH + H⁺.
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option begins at PS I, the third runs backwards, and the fourth places NADP⁺ before PS I.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Electron Transport
solution.final_answer: Option A: H₂O → PS II → electron transport chain (cytochromes) → PS I → NADP⁺

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The bundle sheath cells of C4 plants have a large number of chloroplasts.
Reason (R): Within the mesophyll cells, the chloroplasts align themselves along the walls so that they get the optimum quantity of incident light.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Chloroplasts in two kinds of cells
solution.explanation: Both statements are true. A describes the bundle sheath cells of C4 plants (Kranz anatomy). R describes how chloroplasts are positioned within mesophyll cells in response to light. The positioning of chloroplasts in mesophyll cells says nothing about why bundle sheath cells of C4 plants are rich in chloroplasts, so R does not explain A.
steps: R concerns a different cell type and a different feature
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where does Photosynthesis Take Place?; The C4 Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A plant that has been in bright light is suddenly placed in darkness. Which of the following can continue for some time before stopping?

(a) Carboxylation of RuBP by RuBisCO
(b) Splitting of water
(c) Photophosphorylation
(d) Reduction of PGA using NADPH
(e) Regeneration of RuBP

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Dependence of the biosynthetic phase on light
solution.explanation: The biosynthetic (Calvin) reactions do not directly depend on light; they depend on the ATP and NADPH made in the light reaction. So, immediately after light becomes unavailable, carboxylation, reduction and regeneration continue for some time, using the ATP and NADPH already formed, and then stop. Splitting of water and photophosphorylation are parts of the light reaction and stop when light is withdrawn.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes a light reaction step or leaves out one of the Calvin cycle steps.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where are the ATP and NADPH Used?
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A maize plant and a tomato plant are grown side by side on a hot, brightly lit day. Which outcome is expected, and why?

options.text: Tomato shows the higher rate, because C3 plants have a higher temperature optimum than C4 plants
Both show equal rates, because light is never a limiting factor
Maize stops photosynthesis, because high temperature denatures PEP carboxylase in C4 plants
Maize shows the higher rate of photosynthesis, because C4 plants have a higher temperature optimum, respond to high light intensities and lack photorespiration

solution.concept: C3 and C4 plants under heat and strong light
solution.explanation: C4 plants respond to higher temperatures and show a higher rate of photosynthesis, while C3 plants have a much lower temperature optimum. C4 plants also respond to high light intensities and lack photorespiration, which decreases CO₂ fixation in C3 plants.
steps: Maize: C4 → higher temperature optimum, no photorespiration
solution.why_others_wrong: C3 plants have a lower, not higher, temperature optimum. NCERT does not say light is never limiting (it limits shade plants), and C4 plants are tolerant of high temperatures.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway; Factors Affecting Photosynthesis (Temperature)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Maize shows the higher rate of photosynthesis, because C4 plants have a higher temperature optimum, respond to high light intensities and lack photorespiration

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The splitting of water and the reduction of NADP⁺ take place on the same side of the thylakoid membrane.
Statement II: The protons needed to reduce NADP⁺ to NADPH + H⁺ are removed from the stroma.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The splitting of water takes place on the inner (lumen) side of the thylakoid membrane, so its protons accumulate in the lumen. NADP reductase is located on the stroma side, and the protons needed to reduce NADP⁺ are removed from the stroma. The two events are on opposite sides, which helps build the proton gradient.
steps: Statement I: false, water splitting = lumen side, NADP⁺ reduction = stroma side
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Chemiosmotic Hypothesis
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly traces atmospheric CO₂ through the C4 pathway?

options.text: CO₂ + RuBP → PGA in mesophyll cells → OAA → transported to bundle sheath cells → PEP
CO₂ + PEP → OAA in bundle sheath cells → malic acid → transported to mesophyll cells → CO₂ fixed by RuBisCO
CO₂ + PEP → OAA in mesophyll cells → malic or aspartic acid → transported to bundle sheath cells → CO₂ released → fixed by RuBisCO into PGA
CO₂ + PEP → PGA in mesophyll cells → OAA in bundle sheath cells → RuBP

solution.concept: Path of carbon in the C4 pathway
solution.explanation: In the mesophyll cells, PEPcase fixes CO₂ with PEP to form OAA, a C4 acid. OAA is converted to malic or aspartic acid, which is transported to the bundle sheath cells. There the C4 acid is broken down to release CO₂ and a 3-carbon molecule; the CO₂ enters the Calvin cycle, where RuBisCO fixes it with RuBP to form PGA.
steps: Mesophyll: PEP + CO₂ → OAA → malic/aspartic acid
Bundle sheath: decarboxylation → CO₂ → Calvin cycle
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option uses RuBisCO in the mesophyll, which lacks it. The third places PEPcase in the bundle sheath and RuBisCO in the mesophyll. The fourth makes PGA the product of PEP carboxylation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option C: CO₂ + PEP → OAA in mesophyll cells → malic or aspartic acid → transported to bundle sheath cells → CO₂ released → fixed by RuBisCO into PGA

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In ATP synthase (complex V), the part that is an integral membrane protein complex forming the channel through which protons cross the inner mitochondrial membrane is:

solution.explanation: ATP synthase has two major components, F₁ and F₀. The F₁ headpiece is a peripheral membrane protein complex and contains the site for synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. F₀ is an integral membrane protein complex that forms the channel through which protons cross the inner membrane.
steps: F₁: peripheral headpiece, site of ATP synthesis
solution.why_others_wrong: The F₁ headpiece contains the ATP-synthesising site, not the channel. Cytochrome c and ubiquinone are electron carriers, not parts of ATP synthase.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option C: F₀

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following processes is common to aerobic respiration, alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation?

options.text: Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA

solution.concept: Glycolysis as the common first stage
solution.explanation: In all three, glucose is first broken down to pyruvic acid by glycolysis in the cytoplasm. The fate of pyruvic acid then differs: it is reduced to ethanol and CO₂ or to lactic acid in fermentation, or enters the mitochondria for the link reaction, the TCA cycle and the ETS in aerobic respiration.
steps: Link reaction, TCA cycle, ETS → aerobic respiration only
solution.why_others_wrong: The link reaction, the TCA cycle and the ETS occur only in aerobic respiration.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis; Fermentation; Aerobic Respiration
solution.final_answer: Option B: Glycolysis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Anaerobic organisms can obtain energy from glucose without using oxygen.
Reason (R): All living organisms retain the enzymatic machinery to partially oxidise glucose without the help of oxygen.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The breakdown of glucose to pyruvic acid (glycolysis) does not need oxygen, and all living organisms retain the enzymes for it. In anaerobic organisms glycolysis is the only process of respiration, and it releases some energy as ATP. So R explains A.
steps: R: true; this machinery (glycolysis) is what lets them obtain energy
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the electron transport system, electrons from NADH are oxidised by NADH dehydrogenase (complex I) and transferred to ubiquinone. Ubiquinone is located:

solution.explanation: The ETS is present in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Electrons from NADH produced in the matrix are oxidised by complex I and transferred to ubiquinone located within the inner membrane. Ubiquinone also receives reducing equivalents from FADH₂ through complex II.
solution.why_others_wrong: The outer membrane and the cytoplasm do not carry the ETS. The thylakoid lumen belongs to the chloroplast.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option D: within the inner mitochondrial membrane

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (step of glycolysis) with List-II (what happens).

List-I:
A. Glucose → glucose-6-phosphate
B. Glucose-6-phosphate → fructose-6-phosphate
C. PGAL → 1,3-bisphosphoglyceric acid (BPGA)
D. Phosphoenolpyruvate → pyruvic acid

List-II:
I. Synthesis of ATP
II. Oxidation, with formation of NADH + H⁺
III. Isomerisation
IV. Phosphorylation catalysed by hexokinase

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Glucose is phosphorylated to glucose-6-phosphate by hexokinase, which is then isomerised to fructose-6-phosphate. Later, PGAL is oxidised (two redox equivalents are removed and transferred to NAD⁺, forming NADH + H⁺) and combined with inorganic phosphate to form BPGA. ATP is synthesised when BPGA forms PGA and again when PEP is converted to pyruvic acid.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap isomerisation with oxidation, phosphorylation with isomerisation, or the NADH-forming step with the ATP-forming step.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): CO₂ is released when pyruvic acid is converted to acetyl CoA.
Reason (R): The conversion of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA takes place in the cytoplasm.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Pyruvic acid formed in glycolysis enters the mitochondrial matrix, where it undergoes oxidative decarboxylation by pyruvic dehydrogenase: pyruvic acid + CoA + NAD⁺ → acetyl CoA + CO₂ + NADH + H⁺. So CO₂ is released, but the reaction occurs in the mitochondrial matrix, not the cytoplasm.
steps: R: false, the reaction is in the mitochondrial matrix
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Aerobic Respiration
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
In which of the following conversions is CO₂ released?

(a) Pyruvic acid → acetyl CoA
(b) Formation of α-ketoglutaric acid in the TCA cycle
(c) α-Ketoglutaric acid → succinyl CoA
(d) Succinyl CoA → succinic acid
(e) Pyruvic acid → lactic acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: CO₂ is released in the oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA, and in the two successive decarboxylations of the TCA cycle, which form α-ketoglutaric acid and then succinyl CoA. The conversion of succinyl CoA to succinic acid synthesises GTP, without decarboxylation, and the reduction of pyruvic acid to lactic acid releases no CO₂.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes (d) or (e), or leaves out a decarboxylation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Aerobic Respiration; Tricarboxylic Acid Cycle; Fermentation
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cytochrome c acts as a mobile carrier for the transfer of electrons between complex I and complex III.
Statement II: Ubiquinone receives reducing equivalents from NADH through complex I and from FADH₂ through complex II.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Cytochrome c is a small protein attached to the outer surface of the inner membrane; it acts as a mobile carrier between complex III (cytochrome bc₁ complex) and complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase). Ubiquinone receives reducing equivalents from NADH via complex I and from FADH₂ via complex II; reduced ubiquinone (ubiquinol) is then oxidised by complex III.
steps: Statement I: false, cytochrome c links complex III and complex IV
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of both lactic acid fermentation and alcoholic fermentation?

options.text: Both reoxidise the NADH + H⁺ formed in glycolysis to NAD⁺
Both take place in the mitochondrial matrix
Both release more energy per glucose than aerobic respiration

solution.explanation: In both lactic acid and alcoholic fermentation the reducing agent is NADH + H⁺, which is reoxidised to NAD⁺ as pyruvic acid is reduced. Alcoholic fermentation releases CO₂ (pyruvic acid → CO₂ + ethanol) but lactic acid fermentation does not. Both occur in the cytoplasm, and both release less than seven per cent of the energy in glucose.
solution.why_others_wrong: Lactic acid fermentation releases no CO₂. Fermentation is cytoplasmic. It releases far less energy than aerobic respiration.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Fermentation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both reoxidise the NADH + H⁺ formed in glycolysis to NAD⁺

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
The oxygen supply to a respiring plant cell is completely cut off. Which of the following will stop or decrease?

(a) The flow of electrons through the electron transport system
(b) The continued oxidation of acetyl CoA in the TCA cycle
(c) Glycolysis
(d) The ATP yield per molecule of glucose
(e) The conversion of pyruvic acid to ethanol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Consequences of the absence of oxygen
solution.explanation: Oxygen is the final hydrogen acceptor of the ETS, so without it electron flow stops. The TCA cycle needs continued regeneration of NAD⁺ and FAD⁺ from NADH and FADH₂ in the ETS, so it also stops. Glycolysis does not need oxygen and continues, with NAD⁺ regenerated by fermentation, so pyruvic acid is converted to products such as ethanol. Since only glycolysis yields ATP, the ATP yield per glucose falls.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong combination includes glycolysis or ethanol formation, which continue without oxygen, or leaves out a step that stops.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Fermentation; Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Complex IV, cytochrome c oxidase, contains cytochromes a and a₃ and two copper centres.
Reason (R): The F₁ headpiece of ATP synthase is a peripheral membrane protein complex that contains the site for the synthesis of ATP.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Two components of the inner mitochondrial membrane
solution.explanation: Both statements are true. A describes the composition of complex IV, which passes electrons to oxygen. R describes the F₁ part of ATP synthase (complex V). The structure of ATP synthase has nothing to do with the cytochromes and copper centres of complex IV, so R does not explain A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria from photophosphorylation in chloroplasts?

options.text: In oxidative phosphorylation light energy creates the proton gradient, whereas in photophosphorylation the energy of oxidation-reduction is used
Only photophosphorylation uses an ATP synthase to make ATP
In oxidative phosphorylation the energy of oxidation-reduction is used to create the proton gradient, whereas in photophosphorylation light energy is used
Only oxidative phosphorylation requires a proton gradient across a membrane

solution.explanation: NCERT points out that in photophosphorylation light energy is used to produce the proton gradient needed for phosphorylation, while in respiration the energy of oxidation-reduction is used for the same purpose; hence the name oxidative phosphorylation. Both use a proton gradient across a membrane and an ATP synthase.
steps: Source of energy for the gradient: redox (mitochondria) vs light (chloroplasts)
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option reverses the two. Both processes use ATP synthase and both need a proton gradient.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option C: In oxidative phosphorylation the energy of oxidation-reduction is used to create the proton gradient, whereas in photophosphorylation light energy is used

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: ATP yield from different electron donors
solution.explanation: NCERT states that the number of ATP molecules synthesised depends on the nature of the electron donor: one NADH gives 3 ATP and one FADH₂ gives 2 ATP. The different yields from the two donors are exactly what A states, so R explains A.
steps: R: true; NADH (3 ATP) and FADH₂ (2 ATP) differ in yield
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, spraying a sugarcane crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem and so increases the yield by as much as:

solution.concept: Commercial use of gibberellins in sugarcane
solution.explanation: NCERT: sugarcane stores carbohydrate as sugar in its stem. Spraying the crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, thus increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre.
steps: GA spray lengthens the sugarcane stem
Yield increase: up to 20 tonnes per acre
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 and 200 tonnes are factor-of-ten slips; 20 kilograms per acre changes the unit.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: physiological effects of gibberellins
solution.final_answer: Option A: 20 tonnes per acre

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT illustrates the phases of growth in a root with the 'parallel line technique'. This technique is used to detect:

options.text: The zone of cell division: the root cap is found to have elongated the most
The zone of maturation: the region farthest from the apex is found to have elongated the most
The zone of elongation: the zones immediately behind the apex are found to have elongated the most
Geometric growth: every zone of the root is found to have elongated equally

solution.explanation: Lines are marked at equal distances on a growing root and their spacing is checked after some time. NCERT's figure: detection of zones of elongation by the parallel line technique; the zones immediately behind the apex have elongated most. These lie proximal to the meristematic phase, in the phase of elongation.
steps: Equally spaced marks on a young root
After growth, marks just behind the apex have moved apart the most
That region is the zone of elongation
solution.why_others_wrong: The root cap and the zone of maturation do not show the largest elongation, and the marks do not move apart equally, so the elongation is not uniform along the root.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth: phases of growth
solution.final_answer: Option C: The zone of elongation: the zones immediately behind the apex are found to have elongated the most

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Auxins are generally produced by the growing apices of the stems and roots, from where they migrate to the regions of their action.
Statement II: IAA and IBA are synthetic auxins, whereas NAA and 2,4-D have been isolated from plants.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: auxins are generally produced by the growing apices of the stems and roots, from where they migrate to the regions of their action (Statement I true). Auxins like IAA and indole butyric acid (IBA) have been isolated from plants, while NAA (naphthalene acetic acid) and 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) are synthetic auxins. Statement II swaps the two groups, so it is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: auxins
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the term 'auxin' is applied to:

options.text: Only the indole-3-acetic acid isolated from the tips of oat coleoptiles
Only the synthetic compounds NAA and 2,4-D used as herbicides
All five major groups of plant growth regulators taken together
Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and other natural and synthetic compounds having certain growth-regulating properties

solution.explanation: NCERT: auxin (from the Greek 'auxein', to grow) was first isolated from human urine. The term 'auxin' is applied to indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and to other natural and synthetic compounds having certain growth regulating properties.
steps: Auxin: IAA plus other natural and synthetic compounds
solution.why_others_wrong: The term is not limited to IAA alone or to the synthetic compounds alone, and it does not cover the other PGR groups (gibberellins, cytokinins, ABA, ethylene).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: auxins
solution.final_answer: Option D: Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and other natural and synthetic compounds having certain growth-regulating properties

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT presents the sequence of the developmental process in a plant cell as a flow chart, starting from a meristematic cell. Which order of steps is correct?

options.text: Cell division → expansion (elongation) → plasmatic growth → cell differentiation
Cell division → plasmatic growth → expansion (elongation) → cell differentiation
Plasmatic growth → cell division → cell differentiation → expansion (elongation)
Cell division → cell differentiation → plasmatic growth → expansion (elongation)

solution.concept: Sequence of developmental process in a plant cell
solution.explanation: In NCERT's flow chart, a meristematic cell undergoes cell division, then plasmatic growth (increase in protoplasm), then expansion (elongation), and then cell differentiation, giving a mature cell; a mature cell may later dedifferentiate and redifferentiate. The order matches the phases of growth: meristematic cells rich in protoplasm come first, cells of the elongation zone enlarge and become vacuolated next, and differentiation into mature cells comes last.
steps: Start: cell division in the meristematic cell
Last: cell differentiation to a mature cell
solution.why_others_wrong: Expansion does not come before plasmatic growth, division does not follow plasmatic growth at the start, and differentiation is the last step, not the second.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', development: sequence of the developmental process in a plant cell
solution.final_answer: Option B: Cell division → plasmatic growth → expansion (elongation) → cell differentiation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cytokinins help to delay leaf senescence.
Reason (R): Cytokinins promote nutrient mobilisation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: cytokinins promote nutrient mobilisation, which helps in the delay of leaf senescence. Both statements are true, and the nutrient mobilisation stated in R is the very process through which cytokinins delay senescence (A).
steps: Nutrient mobilisation (R) delays leaf senescence (A): R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: physiological effects of cytokinins
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Ethylene influences horizontal growth of seedlings and swelling of the axis in dicot seedlings.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Ethylene on seedlings; nature of gibberellins
solution.explanation: NCERT: ethylene influences horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of the axis and apical hook formation in dicot seedlings (Statement I true). There are more than 100 gibberellins (GA1, GA2, GA3 and so on) and all GAs are acidic (Statement II true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: gibberellins and ethylene

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (aim of the grower) with List-II (plant growth regulator used, as described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Obtaining parthenocarpic (seedless) tomatoes
B. Making a rosette plant such as cabbage bolt
C. Hastening the ripening of apples with an aqueous spray
D. Promoting adventitious shoot formation

List-II:
I. Ethephon
II. Cytokinin
III. Auxin
IV. Gibberellin

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Auxins induce parthenocarpy, e.g. in tomatoes. Gibberellins promote bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages and other rosette plants. Ethephon, an aqueous solution readily absorbed and transported in the plant, releases ethylene slowly and hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples. Cytokinins help to produce new leaves, chloroplasts, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoot formation.
solution.why_others_wrong: Other codes swap auxin with gibberellin, ethephon with cytokinin, or auxin with ethephon; none of these pairings is given in NCERT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: physiological effects
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT an effect of gibberellins described in NCERT?

options.text: Promoting bolting in beet, cabbages and other plants with a rosette habit
Speeding up the malting process in the brewing industry
Inducing dormancy in seeds and helping them to withstand desiccation
Increasing the length of grape stalks

solution.explanation: NCERT lists for gibberellins: increase in the length of grape stalks, elongation of fruits such as apple, delay of senescence, malting in the brewing industry, increase in sugarcane yield, early seed production in conifers and bolting in rosette plants. Inducing seed dormancy and helping seeds to withstand desiccation are roles of abscisic acid, which in most situations acts as an antagonist to gibberellins.
steps: Bolting, malting and grape stalk elongation: gibberellins
Seed dormancy and desiccation tolerance: abscisic acid
solution.why_others_wrong: Bolting, malting and the elongation of grape stalks are all effects of gibberellins named in NCERT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: gibberellins and abscisic acid
solution.final_answer: Option C: Inducing dormancy in seeds and helping them to withstand desiccation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Each statement below credits one plant growth regulator with two effects. In which statements are BOTH effects correctly assigned according to NCERT?

(a) Auxin: initiates rooting in stem cuttings and induces parthenocarpy in tomatoes.
(b) Gibberellin: increases the length of grape stalks and speeds up the malting process.
(c) Cytokinin: helps to overcome apical dominance and promotes adventitious shoot formation.
(d) Ethylene: initiates germination in peanut seeds and stimulates the closure of stomata.
(e) Abscisic acid: inhibits seed germination and promotes female flowers in cucumbers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Matching paired effects to one PGR
solution.explanation: (a) Both are auxin effects. (b) Both are gibberellin effects. (c) Both are cytokinin effects. (d) Ethylene does break seed and bud dormancy and initiates germination in peanut seeds, but the closure of stomata is stimulated by abscisic acid, so (d) is wrong. (e) Abscisic acid does inhibit seed germination, but promoting female flowers in cucumbers is an ethylene effect, so (e) is wrong.
steps: (d): stomatal closure is ABA, not ethylene
(e): female flowers in cucumber is ethylene, not ABA
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong option includes (d) or (e), each of which pairs one correct effect with an effect of a different PGR; '(b), (c) and (d) only' also leaves out the correct (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: physiological effects
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Spraying juvenile conifers with gibberellins leads to early seed production.
Reason (R): Gibberellins are used to speed up the malting process in the brewing industry.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: spraying juvenile conifers with GAs hastens the maturity period, thus leading to early seed production (A true). Gibberellins are also used to speed up the malting process in the brewing industry (R true). R is a different application of the same hormone in a different setting; malting has nothing to do with why conifers mature early, so R does not explain A.
steps: A: true (GAs hasten the maturity period)
R is an unrelated use: not the explanation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: physiological effects of gibberellins
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: F. Skoog observed that callus from the internodal segments of tobacco stems proliferated only if, in addition to auxins, the nutrient medium contained extracts such as yeast extract or coconut milk. According to NCERT, which naturally occurring plant growth regulator was later isolated from coconut milk?

solution.concept: From Skoog's observation to natural cytokinins
solution.explanation: Skoog and Miller later crystallised the cytokinesis-promoting substance and named it kinetin, but kinetin was obtained from autoclaved herring sperm DNA and does not occur naturally in plants. The search for natural substances with cytokinin-like activity led to the isolation of zeatin from corn kernels and coconut milk.
steps: Coconut milk supported cell division in tobacco callus
Kinetin: from autoclaved herring sperm DNA, not natural
Natural cytokinin from corn kernels and coconut milk: zeatin
solution.why_others_wrong: Kinetin came from autoclaved herring sperm DNA and does not occur naturally in plants; IBA and GA₃ are not described as isolated from coconut milk.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Abscisic acid and its relation to gibberellins
solution.explanation: NCERT: ABA plays an important role in seed development, maturation and dormancy; by inducing dormancy it helps seeds to withstand desiccation (Statement I true). NCERT adds that in most situations ABA acts as an antagonist to GAs, not synergistically (Statement II false).
steps: ABA and GAs: antagonists in most situations

solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT states that the mitotic divisions leading from the functional megaspore to the 8-nucleate embryo sac are strictly free nuclear. This means that:

options.text: Each nuclear division is immediately followed by cell wall formation
The nuclear divisions are not followed immediately by cell wall formation
The divisions are meiotic, so the chromosome number is halved at each step
The nuclei divide without any replication of their DNA

solution.concept: Free-nuclear divisions in the embryo sac
solution.explanation: NCERT: the nucleus of the functional megaspore divides mitotically to form two nuclei, which move to opposite poles; two more sequential mitotic nuclear divisions give the 4-nucleate and 8-nucleate stages. These mitotic divisions are strictly free nuclear, that is, nuclear divisions are not followed immediately by cell wall formation. Walls form only later, around six of the eight nuclei.
steps: Free nuclear = nuclei divide, walls do not form at once
The divisions are mitotic, not meiotic
solution.why_others_wrong: Immediate wall formation is the opposite of free-nuclear division; the divisions are mitotic (the megaspore is already haploid), and mitosis involves DNA replication.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pistil, megasporangium and embryo sac: megasporogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: The nuclear divisions are not followed immediately by cell wall formation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Of the eight nuclei present in a typical mature angiosperm embryo sac, how many are surrounded by cell walls and organised into cells?

solution.concept: Cellular organisation of the embryo sac
solution.explanation: NCERT: six of the eight nuclei are surrounded by cell walls and organised into cells (three in the egg apparatus and three antipodals); the remaining two nuclei, called polar nuclei, lie below the egg apparatus in the large central cell. Hence the embryo sac is 7-celled (six cells plus the central cell) but 8-nucleate.
steps: Two polar nuclei share the central cell
solution.why_others_wrong: Seven is the number of cells (it counts the binucleate central cell); eight is the number of nuclei; three counts only one group of cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pistil, megasporangium and embryo sac: female gametophyte
solution.final_answer: Option D: Six

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a few species, the thalamus also contributes to fruit formation, giving false fruits. Which of the following is named in NCERT as such a species?

solution.explanation: NCERT: in a few species such as apple, strawberry and cashew, the thalamus also contributes to fruit formation; such fruits are called false fruits. Most fruits develop only from the ovary and are true fruits.
solution.why_others_wrong: Mango, orange and guava are NCERT's examples of fruits with a fleshy pericarp developed from the ovary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: structures and events, fruit
solution.final_answer: Option A: Strawberry

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mature seeds of crop plants can be stored for long periods and used to raise a crop in the next season.
Reason (R): As a seed matures, it becomes dehydrated, with only about 10–15 per cent moisture by mass, and its embryo may enter a state of inactivity called dormancy.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: as the seed matures its water content is reduced (10–15 per cent moisture by mass), general metabolic activity slows down and the embryo may enter dormancy. It then states that dehydration and dormancy of mature seeds are crucial for the storage of seeds, which can be used as food throughout the year and to raise a crop in the next season. R gives exactly this cause of A.
steps: Dehydration and dormancy make storage possible: R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: seed
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: After reaching the ovary, the pollen tube enters the ovule through the micropyle.
Statement II: The pollen tube then enters one of the antipodal cells through the filiform apparatus and releases the two male gametes into it.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: after reaching the ovary, the pollen tube enters the ovule through the micropyle and then enters one of the synergids through the filiform apparatus, releasing the two male gametes into the cytoplasm of the synergid. questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. Chasmogamous flowers
B. Cleistogamous flowers
C. Geitonogamy
D. Xenogamy

List-II:
I. Transfer of pollen grains to the stigma of a different plant
II. Flowers that do not open at all
III. Flowers with exposed anthers and stigma, similar to the flowers of other species
IV. Transfer of pollen grains to the stigma of another flower of the same plant

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Kinds of flowers and of pollination
solution.explanation: Chasmogamous flowers are similar to the flowers of other species, with exposed anthers and stigma. Cleistogamous flowers do not open at all. Geitonogamy is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant. Xenogamy is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a different plant.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap chasmogamous with cleistogamous flowers or geitonogamy with xenogamy.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: kinds of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The pericarp of a fruit may be fleshy or dry. Which pair is named in NCERT as fruits with a fleshy pericarp?

solution.explanation: NCERT: the fruit develops from the ovary and its wall forms the pericarp. The pericarp is fleshy as in guava, orange and mango, or may be dry, as in groundnut and mustard.
solution.why_others_wrong: Groundnut and mustard both have a dry pericarp; the other two pairs mix one fleshy and one dry example.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: fruit
solution.final_answer: Option C: Guava and mango

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A flowering plant has 2n = 20. Assuming normal monosporic development, what is the total number of chromosomes in all the nuclei of one mature embryo sac taken together, and the number of chromosomes in one cell of the endosperm formed after fertilisation?

solution.concept: Ploidy of the female gametophyte and the endosperm
solution.explanation: The functional megaspore is formed by meiosis, so it and all eight nuclei derived from it by mitosis are haploid (n = 10). Total in the embryo sac = 8 × 10 = 80. The endosperm develops from the primary endosperm nucleus, formed by the fusion of two polar nuclei with a male gamete, so it is triploid: 3 × 10 = 30.
solution.why_others_wrong: 160 treats the embryo-sac nuclei as diploid; 70 counts 7 cells instead of 8 nuclei; 20 is the diploid number, not the triploid endosperm.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pistil, megasporangium and embryo sac; double fertilisation
solution.final_answer: Option B: 80 and 30

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about pollination by water are correct?

(a) Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons.
(b) Vallisneria and Hydrilla grow in fresh water, while Zostera is a marine sea-grass.
(c) In water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind.
(d) In Zostera, the female flowers reach the water surface on long stalks.
(e) Water-pollinated flowers are usually colourful and produce nectar.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: (a), (b) and (c) are NCERT statements: water pollination is rare (about 30 genera, mostly monocots); Vallisneria and Hydrilla are freshwater, Zostera is a marine sea-grass; not all aquatic plants use water, since in water hyacinth and water lily the flowers emerge above water and are pollinated by insects or wind. (d) is false: in sea-grasses the female flowers remain submerged and the pollen is released inside the water; the female flower reaching the surface on a long stalk is Vallisneria. (e) is false: wind- and water-pollinated flowers are not very colourful and do not produce nectar.
steps: (e): such flowers lack colour and nectar
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) include a false statement; '(b), (d) and (e)' also drops (a) and (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: agents of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Unisexual flowers on a monoecious plant such as castor or maize prevent autogamy but not geitonogamy.
Reason (R): In a monoecious plant, both male and female flowers are present on the same plant.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: production of unisexual flowers is an outbreeding device. If both male and female flowers are present on the same plant, as in castor and maize (monoecious), it prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy. Because each flower is unisexual, pollen cannot reach the stigma of its own flower (no autogamy); but because male and female flowers are on the same plant (R), pollen can reach a female flower of the same plant (geitonogamy). R explains why geitonogamy is still possible.
steps: Male and female flowers on one plant allow geitonogamy: R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', outbreeding devices
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In plants that shed pollen at the two-celled stage, the generative cell divides to form the two male gametes during the growth of the pollen tube.
Statement II: The intine of the pollen grain is made of sporopollenin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in plants that shed pollen in the 2-celled condition, the generative cell divides and forms the two male gametes during the growth of the pollen tube in the stigma (Statement I true). The pollen grain has a hard outer exine made of sporopollenin and a thin, continuous inner intine made of cellulose and pectin (Statement II false).
steps: Exine: sporopollenin; intine: cellulose and pectin
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: After double fertilisation in a typical embryo sac, how many of its cells degenerate, and which cells develop further?

options.text: Three (the antipodals); the zygote, the primary endosperm cell and both synergids develop further
Two (the synergids); the zygote, the primary endosperm cell and the antipodals develop further
Seven (all of them); new cells arise from the integuments
Five (two synergids and three antipodals); the zygote and the primary endosperm cell develop further

solution.concept: Fate of the cells of the embryo sac
solution.explanation: Syngamy turns the egg into the zygote (which develops into the embryo), and triple fusion turns the central cell into the primary endosperm cell (which develops into the endosperm). NCERT: the synergids and antipodals degenerate after fertilisation. A 7-celled embryo sac therefore loses 2 synergids + 3 antipodals = 5 cells.
steps: Central cell → primary endosperm cell → endosperm
solution.why_others_wrong: Both synergids and all three antipodals degenerate, so counts of 3 or 2 are incomplete; the zygote and the primary endosperm cell do not degenerate.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', double fertilisation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Five (two synergids and three antipodals); the zygote and the primary endosperm cell develop further

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure of the seed or fruit) with List-II (structure from which it develops or remains).

List-I:
A. Seed coat
B. Perisperm
C. Pericarp
D. Endosperm

List-II:
I. Primary endosperm cell
II. Ovary wall
III. Integuments
IV. Nucellus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Origin of seed and fruit parts
solution.explanation: NCERT: the integuments of the ovule harden as tough protective seed coats. In some seeds, such as black pepper and beet, remnants of the nucellus persist; this residual, persistent nucellus is the perisperm. The wall of the ovary develops into the wall of the fruit, the pericarp. The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly to form the triploid endosperm tissue.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the origins of the seed coat and perisperm, of the pericarp and endosperm, or of the seed coat and pericarp.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: structures and events
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the embryo are correct?

(a) A typical dicotyledonous embryo consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons.
(b) In the grass embryo, the coleorhiza encloses the plumule.
(c) The single cotyledon of the grass family is called the scutellum.
(d) The embryo develops from the primary endosperm cell.
(e) In the grass embryo, the epicotyl has a shoot apex and a few leaf primordia enclosed in a hollow foliar structure, the coleoptile.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Structure of dicot and monocot embryos
solution.explanation: (a) True. (b) False: the coleorhiza is an undifferentiated sheath enclosing the radicle and root cap. (c) True: the embryo of monocots has one cotyledon, called the scutellum in the grass family. (d) False: the embryo develops from the zygote; the primary endosperm cell forms the endosperm. (e) True.
steps: (b): coleorhiza encloses radicle and root cap
solution.why_others_wrong: Options including (b) or (d) include a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: embryo

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A species of moth and the plant Yucca cannot complete their life cycles without each other.
Reason (R): The moth deposits its eggs in the locule of the ovary, the flower in turn gets pollinated by the moth, and the moth larvae come out of the eggs as the seeds start developing.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in some species the floral reward is a safe place to lay eggs. A similar relationship exists between a species of moth and Yucca, where both cannot complete their life cycles without each other: the moth deposits its eggs in the locule of the ovary, the flower is pollinated by the moth, and the larvae emerge as the seeds develop. The plant depends on the moth for pollination and the moth on the developing ovary for its larvae, so R explains A.
steps: Pollination by the moth and egg-laying in the ovary make each depend on the other
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: agents of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A breeder crosses two varieties of a plant with bisexual flowers. Which sequence of steps, as described in NCERT, must be followed for the female parent?

options.text: Bagging → emasculation after the anthers dehisce → dusting of pollen from the male parent → rebagging
Emasculation of the flower bud before the anthers dehisce → bagging → dusting of pollen from the male parent when the stigma becomes receptive → rebagging
Emasculation → dusting of pollen from the male parent → bagging after the fruit sets
Dusting of pollen from the male parent → emasculation → bagging → rebagging

solution.explanation: NCERT: if the female parent bears bisexual flowers, the anthers are removed from the flower bud before they dehisce (emasculation); the emasculated flower is covered with a bag, generally of butter paper, to prevent contamination by unwanted pollen (bagging); when the stigma attains receptivity, mature pollen collected from the male parent is dusted on it and the flower is rebagged and the fruit allowed to develop.
steps: Dust selected pollen on the receptive stigma
solution.why_others_wrong: Emasculating after dehiscence allows self-pollen to reach the stigma; leaving the flower unbagged until fruit set allows contamination; dusting pollen before emasculation makes self-pollination possible.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', artificial hybridisation
solution.final_answer: Option B: Emasculation of the flower bud before the anthers dehisce → bagging → dusting of pollen from the male parent when the stigma becomes receptive → rebagging

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A seed of black pepper has been formed after cross-pollination and normal double fertilisation. Which pair of its tissues is genetically identical to each other?

options.text: The perisperm and the seed coat
The embryo and the seed coat

solution.concept: Maternal and filial tissues of a seed
solution.explanation: The perisperm is the persistent remnant of the nucellus, and the seed coat develops from the integuments; both are diploid tissues of the mother plant formed without fertilisation, so they are genetically identical (both carry the mother's genotype). The embryo (from the zygote: egg + one male gamete) and the endosperm (from the primary endosperm nucleus: two polar nuclei + the other male gamete) carry paternal genes and differ from each other in ploidy (2n and 3n).
steps: Embryo and endosperm include paternal genes and differ in ploidy
solution.why_others_wrong: Embryo (2n) and endosperm (3n) differ in ploidy; the embryo carries paternal genes while the maternal seed coat does not; the endosperm (3n, with paternal genes) differs from the maternal perisperm (2n).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: seed
solution.final_answer: Option B: The perisperm and the seed coat

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) In a dioecious species such as papaya, every seed formed by sexual reproduction results from xenogamy.
(b) Geitonogamy brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma.
(c) Cleistogamous flowers produce assured seed set even in the absence of pollinators.
(d) In a monoecious plant such as maize, geitonogamy can occur.
(e) Self-incompatibility prevents autogamy but still allows pollen from other flowers of the same plant to fertilise the ovules.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Consequences of the different pollination patterns
solution.explanation: (a) True: dioecy prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy, so the pollen must come from a different plant. (b) False: geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination but genetically similar to autogamy, since the pollen comes from the same plant; only xenogamy brings genetically different pollen. (c) True. (d) True: monoecy prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy. (e) False: self-incompatibility prevents self-pollen, from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant, from fertilising the ovules.
steps: (b): geitonogamy pollen is from the same plant
(e): self-incompatibility blocks pollen of the same plant too
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (b) or (e) include a false statement; '(c), (d) and (e)' also drops the true (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination; outbreeding devices
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Because the egg and the two polar nuclei of an embryo sac are genetically identical, the embryo and the endosperm of a seed always have the same genotype.
Reason (R): The two male gametes of a pollen grain are formed by the mitotic division of a single generative cell.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: R is true: the generative cell divides mitotically to give the two male gametes, so they carry the same alleles. The egg and polar nuclei are indeed identical, but A's conclusion is false: the embryo comes from one egg + one male gamete (2n), whereas the endosperm comes from two polar nuclei + one male gamete (3n). For example, in aa (female) × AA (male), the embryo is Aa but the endosperm is aaA. So A is false and R is true.
steps: Different dosage, so different genotype: A false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain; double fertilisation
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (part related to a seed from the cross aa (female parent) × AA (male parent)) with List-II (its genotype).

List-I:
A. Seed coat
B. Endosperm
C. Embryo
D. Vegetative cell of the pollen grain that fertilised the ovule

List-II:
I. Aa
II. A
III. aa
IV. aaA

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Genotypes of maternal tissue, endosperm, embryo and male gametophyte
solution.explanation: The seed coat develops from the integuments of the mother plant: aa. The pollen of the AA male parent is haploid, so its vegetative cell and both male gametes carry A. Egg (a) + male gamete (A) gives the embryo Aa. Two polar nuclei (a + a) + male gamete (A) give the endosperm aaA.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes give the seed coat a paternal allele, swap the embryo and endosperm, or treat the haploid vegetative cell as triploid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', double fertilisation; post-fertilisation: seed
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A plant of genotype Aa reproduces in different ways. Which of the following is NOT expected to give offspring that are all genetically identical to this mother plant?

options.text: Seeds formed by apomixis, as in some Asteraceae and grasses
Nucellar embryos that arise from diploid nucellar cells protruding into the embryo sac
Seeds from its cleistogamous flowers, formed by self-fertilisation
An embryo that develops without fertilisation from a diploid egg cell formed without reduction division

solution.explanation: In apomixis, seeds form without fertilisation: e.g. a diploid egg formed without reduction division develops into an embryo, or nucellar cells develop into embryos. No meiosis and no fertilisation means no segregation, so all such offspring are Aa. Cleistogamous flowers are autogamous: meiosis gives A and a gametes, and self-fertilisation gives AA, Aa and aa offspring, so not all are identical to the mother.
steps: Apomictic and nucellar embryos: no segregation, all Aa
Cleistogamy: autogamy with meiosis and fertilisation
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are forms of apomixis, which NCERT describes as asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction; the embryo forms without meiosis and fertilisation, so there is no segregation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', apomixis and polyembryony; pollination: kinds of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option C: Seeds from its cleistogamous flowers, formed by self-fertilisation

(c) The nucellus is tissue of the ovule of the diploid parent: diploid. (d) The generative cell arises by mitosis of the haploid microspore: haploid. (e) The synergid is part of the female gametophyte, formed by mitosis from the haploid megaspore: haploid.

Assertion (A): Seeds of wheat are albuminous.
