questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A person who regularly takes in more food than the body uses immediately tends to accumulate fat beneath the skin.
Reason (R): The excess of nutrients which are not used immediately are converted into fats and stored in adipose tissue, which is located mainly beneath the skin.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin. Its cells are specialised to store fats. The excess of nutrients which are not used immediately are converted into fats and are stored in this tissue. This directly explains why surplus food intake builds up fat beneath the skin.
steps: Excess nutrients → fat → stored in adipose beneath skin → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because the storage of surplus nutrients as fat in subcutaneous adipose tissue is the cause of the Assertion; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: connective tissue (adipose tissue)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cells, tissues, organs and organ systems split up the work in a way that exhibits division of labour and contribute to the survival of the body as a whole.
Statement II: Each organ such as the stomach, lung, heart or kidney is formed from a single type of tissue.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: tissues are organised in specific proportion and pattern to form an organ like the stomach, lung, heart and kidney – that is, an organ is built of several tissues. Cells, tissues, organs and organ systems split up the work in a way that exhibits division of labour and contribute to the survival of the body as a whole.
steps: Statement II → false (organs contain tissues in a specific proportion and pattern)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept the single-tissue claim; B rejects NCERT's statement of division of labour.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', organ and organ system
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A tissue taken from the wall of the intestine shows spindle-shaped fibres that taper at both ends, show no striations, are held together by cell junctions and are bundled in a connective tissue sheath. Which of the following statements about this tissue are correct?

(a) It is smooth muscle tissue.
(b) The same type of tissue occurs in the walls of blood vessels and the stomach.
(c) Its contraction can be directly controlled by thinking about it.
(d) It is described as involuntary muscle.
(e) Its cells are joined by communication junctions (intercalated discs) like those of the heart.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: smooth muscle fibres taper at both ends (fusiform) and do not show striations. Cell junctions hold them together and they are bundled together in a connective tissue sheath. The walls of internal organs such as the blood vessels, stomach and intestine contain this tissue. Smooth muscles are involuntary, as their functioning cannot be directly controlled. Communication junctions (intercalated discs) are described for cardiac muscle.
steps: (e) false – intercalated discs belong to cardiac muscle
solution.why_others_wrong: A includes (c) and leaves out (b); C adds the cardiac-muscle feature (e); D includes (c) and (e) and leaves out (a) and (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: muscle tissue
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the frog, air drawn in through the nostrils passes into the buccal cavity and then to the lungs.
Reason (R): On land, the skin is the only respiratory organ of the frog.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the lungs of the frog are a pair of elongated, pink-coloured sac-like structures in the upper part of the trunk (thorax). Air enters through the nostrils into the buccal cavity and then to the lungs. On land, the buccal cavity, skin and lungs all act as respiratory organs, so the skin is not the only one.
steps: R false – buccal cavity, skin and lungs on land
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B accept the false Reason; D rejects the NCERT route of air into the lungs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: anatomy (respiratory system)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure in the frog) with List-II (organ system it belongs to).

List-I:
A. Conus arteriosus
B. Optic lobes
C. Gall bladder
D. Lungs

List-II:
I. Neural system
II. Respiratory system
III. Digestive system
IV. Circulatory system

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the ventricle of the frog's heart opens into a sac-like conus arteriosus (circulatory system); the mid-brain is characterised by a pair of optic lobes (neural system); the gall bladder stores bile secreted by the liver (digestive system); the lungs are the organs of pulmonary respiration (respiratory system).
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps the optic lobes and the gall bladder; B swaps the conus arteriosus and the lungs; C swaps the conus arteriosus and the optic lobes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: anatomy
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: NCERT mentions microvilli on the free surface of two kinds of simple epithelium. Which pair is it?

solution.explanation: NCERT: the cuboidal epithelium of the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron has microvilli, and the free surface of columnar epithelium may have microvilli. Squamous epithelium is a thin layer of flattened cells forming a diffusion boundary, and compound epithelium is protective.
steps: Columnar → free surface may have microvilli
solution.why_others_wrong: A, C and D each include squamous or compound epithelium, for which NCERT mentions no microvilli.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: epithelial tissue
solution.final_answer: Option B: Cuboidal and columnar epithelium

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Of the three specialised connective tissues – cartilage, bone and blood – only bone has a hard, non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts.
Statement II: In blood, as in the other connective tissues, the cells secrete fibres of the structural proteins collagen or elastin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: bones have a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres; the intercellular material of cartilage is solid and pliable; blood is a fluid connective tissue. NCERT also states that in all connective tissues except blood, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.
steps: Statement II → false (blood is the exception)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept Statement II, ignoring NCERT's 'except blood'; B rejects Statement I, though cartilage is pliable and blood is fluid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: connective tissue
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following surfaces are covered or lined by compound epithelium, according to NCERT?

(a) The dry surface of the skin
(b) The moist surface of the buccal cavity
(c) The inner lining of the pancreatic ducts
(d) The walls of the air sacs of the lungs
(e) The tubular parts of the nephrons

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: compound epithelium covers the dry surface of the skin, the moist surface of the buccal cavity and the pharynx, and the inner lining of the ducts of salivary glands and of pancreatic ducts. The walls of the air sacs of the lungs are lined by squamous epithelium and the tubular parts of nephrons by cuboidal epithelium.
solution.why_others_wrong: A leaves out the pancreatic ducts; B adds the nephron tubules (cuboidal); C adds the air sacs (squamous) and leaves out the skin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: epithelial tissue (compound epithelium)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A student compares the frog with human beings. Which of the following statements are correct according to NCERT?

(a) Both have a closed type of blood vascular system.
(b) The heart of the frog has three chambers, whereas the human heart has four.
(c) The RBCs of the frog are nucleated, whereas human RBCs are devoid of a nucleus.
(d) Both have a hepatic portal system connecting the intestine with the liver.
(e) Like human beings, the frog maintains a constant body temperature.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the vascular system of the frog is a well-developed closed type, the heart has three chambers (two atria and one ventricle), its RBCs are nucleated and contain haemoglobin, and it has a hepatic portal system between the liver and the intestine. Humans also have a closed circulatory system, a four-chambered heart, RBCs devoid of a nucleus (as in most mammals) and a hepatic portal vein carrying blood from the intestine to the liver. The frog, however, is cold-blooded (poikilotherm).
solution.why_others_wrong: B and C include (e), though the frog is cold-blooded; D leaves out the correct statement (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: anatomy (circulatory system); Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', erythrocytes and double circulation
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (epithelium) with List-II (sites where NCERT says it is found).

List-I:
A. Ciliated epithelium
B. Cuboidal epithelium
C. Columnar epithelium
D. Squamous epithelium

List-II:
I. Lining of the stomach and intestine
II. Walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs
III. Inner surface of bronchioles and fallopian tubes
IV. Ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: ciliated epithelium is mainly present on the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes; cuboidal epithelium is commonly found in the ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons; columnar epithelium lines the stomach and intestine; squamous epithelium is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps cuboidal and columnar; B swaps ciliated and cuboidal; C swaps ciliated and squamous.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: epithelial tissue (simple epithelium)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The cartilage at the tip of the nose can be pressed and bent without being crushed.
Reason (R): The intercellular material of cartilage is solid and pliable and resists compression.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the intercellular material of cartilage is solid and pliable and resists compression; in adults, cartilage is present in the tip of the nose, outer ear joints, between adjacent bones of the vertebral column, limbs and hands. Pliability lets the nose tip bend, and resistance to compression keeps it from being crushed, so R explains A.
steps: Pliable + resists compression → bends without crushing → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because the pliable, compression-resistant matrix is the reason for the behaviour described; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissues: connective tissue (cartilage)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Amino acids differ in their R group. The amino acid whose R group is simply a hydrogen atom is:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the R group in proteinaceous amino acids could be a hydrogen (the amino acid is called glycine), a methyl group (alanine), hydroxy methyl (serine), etc.
solution.why_others_wrong: Alanine has a methyl R group and serine a hydroxy methyl R group; valine is cited by NCERT as a neutral amino acid, not one with H as its R group.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', amino acids
solution.final_answer: Option A: Glycine

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: For which kind of enzyme co-factor does NCERT say that its association with the apoenzyme is only transient, usually occurring during the course of catalysis?

solution.explanation: NCERT: co-factors are of three kinds – prosthetic groups, co-enzymes and metal ions. Prosthetic groups are organic compounds distinguished from other co-factors in that they are tightly bound to the apoenzyme (e.g. haem in peroxidase and catalase). Co-enzymes are also organic compounds, but their association with the apoenzyme is only transient, usually occurring during the course of catalysis.
solution.why_others_wrong: Prosthetic groups, including haem, are tightly bound; metal ions act by forming coordination bonds with side chains at the active site, and NCERT does not describe them as the transiently associated organic co-factor.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: co-factors
solution.final_answer: Option B: Co-enzymes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A nitrogenous base attached to a sugar is called a nucleoside.
Statement II: Adenylic acid and guanylic acid are nucleosides.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: a nitrogenous base attached to a sugar is a nucleoside (adenosine, guanosine, thymidine, uridine, cytidine). If a phosphate group is also esterified to the 5′-OH of the sugar, it is a nucleotide; adenylic acid, thymidylic acid, guanylic acid, uridylic acid and cytidylic acid are nucleotides.
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept the '-ylic acids' as nucleosides, though they carry a phosphate; B rejects NCERT's definition of a nucleoside.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', nucleic acids
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (nitrogenous base) with List-II (nucleoside formed with it).

List-I:
A. Adenine
B. Guanine
C. Thymine
D. Uracil

List-II:
I. Uridine
II. Thymidine
III. Adenosine
IV. Guanosine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: a nitrogenous base attached to a sugar is a nucleoside; adenosine, guanosine, thymidine, uridine and cytidine are nucleosides, formed from adenine, guanine, thymine, uracil and cytosine respectively.
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps the two purines; B swaps the two pyrimidines; D swaps adenine and thymine.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', nucleic acids
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (amino acid) with List-II (nature as described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Glutamic acid
B. Lysine
C. Valine
D. Phenylalanine

List-II:
I. Aromatic
II. Neutral
III. Basic
IV. Acidic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: based on the number of amino and carboxyl groups, there are acidic (e.g. glutamic acid), basic (lysine) and neutral (valine) amino acids. Similarly, there are aromatic amino acids (tyrosine, phenylalanine and tryptophan).
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps acidic and basic; B swaps lysine and valine; C swaps valine and phenylalanine.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', amino acids
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Carboxypeptidase is a proteolytic enzyme: it breaks peptide bonds of proteins by adding water. In NCERT's classification of enzymes, it belongs to the class:

solution.concept: Classifying an enzyme by its reaction
solution.explanation: NCERT: hydrolases catalyse the hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic, C–C, C–halide or P–N bonds. Carboxypeptidase (for which NCERT names zinc as a co-factor) is proteolytic, i.e. it hydrolyses peptide bonds, so it is a hydrolase.
steps: Peptide bond broken by hydrolysis → hydrolase
solution.why_others_wrong: Transferases move a group G between two substrates; lyases remove groups by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds; ligases link two compounds together.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: classification and nomenclature; co-factors
solution.final_answer: Option C: Hydrolases

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cellulose does not give a blue colour when treated with iodine.
Reason (R): Cellulose does not contain complex helices and hence cannot hold I₂ molecules.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: starch forms helical secondary structures and can hold I₂ molecules in the helical portion; the starch–I₂ complex is blue. Cellulose does not contain complex helices and hence cannot hold I₂. The blue colour depends on I₂ held in the helix, so the absence of helices explains the absence of colour.
steps: No helix → no I₂ held → no blue colour → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because inability to hold I₂ is precisely why cellulose stays uncoloured; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', polysaccharides
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): DNA ligase, which joins two DNA fragments by forming P–O bonds between them, is placed in the class Ligases.
Reason (R): Ligases catalyse the linking together of two compounds, for example the joining of C–O, C–S, C–N or P–O bonds.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT defines ligases as enzymes catalysing the linking together of two compounds, e.g. enzymes which catalyse the joining of C–O, C–S, C–N, P–O, etc. bonds. DNA ligase links two DNA fragments by forming P–O bonds, which fits this definition exactly.
steps: Joining two compounds via P–O bond = ligase reaction → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because the class definition in R is what places DNA ligase among the ligases; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: classification and nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An enzyme that requires a co-factor loses its catalytic activity when the co-factor is removed.
Reason (R): Co-factors are the protein constituents of such enzymes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: enzymes may be composed of one or several polypeptide chains; in many cases non-protein constituents called co-factors are bound to the enzyme to make it catalytically active. The protein portion is called the apoenzyme. When the co-factor is removed from the enzyme, the catalytic activity of the enzyme is lost. So the Assertion is true, but co-factors are non-protein constituents.
steps: R false – co-factors are non-protein; the protein part is the apoenzyme
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B accept the false Reason; D rejects NCERT's statement that activity is lost on removing the co-factor.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: co-factors
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The activity of an enzyme declines both below and above its optimum temperature.
Statement II: In the presence of a competitive inhibitor, the substrate can still bind normally to the enzyme, because the inhibitor binds to a site other than the substrate-binding site.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: each enzyme shows its highest activity at a particular temperature and pH (the optimum); activity declines both below and above the optimum value. A competitive inhibitor closely resembles the substrate and, owing to this similarity, competes with the substrate for the substrate-binding site, so the substrate cannot bind and enzyme action declines.
steps: Statement II → false (the inhibitor competes for the substrate-binding site)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept Statement II, which describes the opposite of competitive inhibition; B rejects NCERT's statement about the optimum temperature.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: factors affecting enzyme activity
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Peroxidase uses H₂O₂ to oxidise another substrate, the H₂O₂ itself being reduced to water. In NCERT's classification of enzymes, peroxidase belongs to the class:

solution.explanation: NCERT: oxidoreductases/dehydrogenases catalyse oxido-reduction between two substrates S and S′: S reduced + S′ oxidised → S oxidised + S′ reduced. In the peroxidase reaction one substrate is oxidised while H₂O₂ is reduced, which is exactly this pattern. (NCERT also names haem as the prosthetic group of peroxidase.)
steps: One substrate oxidised + the other reduced → oxidoreductase
solution.why_others_wrong: Hydrolases split bonds by adding water; transferases move a group other than hydrogen; isomerases inter-convert isomers – none describes a redox reaction between two substrates.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: classification and nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option D: Oxidoreductases

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (level of protein structure) with List-II (description in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Primary
B. Secondary
C. Tertiary
D. Quaternary

List-II:
I. Long chain folded upon itself like a hollow woollen ball
II. Arrangement of individually folded subunits with respect to each other
III. Sequence of amino acids, i.e. the positional information in a protein
IV. Portions of the thread arranged as a helix, like a revolving staircase

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the primary structure is the sequence of amino acids (the positional information); in the secondary structure only some portions of the protein thread are arranged as a helix, similar to a revolving staircase; in the tertiary structure the long chain is folded upon itself like a hollow woollen ball; the quaternary structure is the manner in which individually folded polypeptides or subunits are arranged with respect to each other (e.g. adult haemoglobin).
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps secondary and tertiary; C swaps primary and secondary; D swaps tertiary and quaternary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', proteins: structure of proteins
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lecithin is a triglyceride.
Reason (R): Lecithin is a phospholipid: besides glycerol and fatty acids, it contains phosphorus and a phosphorylated organic compound.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: fatty acids esterified with glycerol form monoglycerides, diglycerides and triglycerides (fats and oils). Some lipids have phosphorus and a phosphorylated organic compound in them; these are phospholipids, found in cell membranes, and lecithin is one example. So lecithin is not a triglyceride; the Reason is true.
steps: A false – lecithin is a phospholipid
solution.why_others_wrong: A, B and C treat the Assertion as true, but a triglyceride has only glycerol esterified with three fatty acids.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', lipids
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An enzyme molecule is used up when it converts one molecule of substrate into product.
Reason (R): After the products are released from the enzyme–product complex, the free enzyme is ready to bind another molecule of substrate and run through the catalytic cycle once again.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT describes the catalytic cycle: the substrate binds the active site, the enzyme alters its shape to fit more tightly, the substrate's bonds are broken and an enzyme–product complex forms, and the products are released. The free enzyme is then ready to bind another substrate molecule and run through the cycle again. Hence the enzyme is not used up; the Assertion is false.
steps: A false – the enzyme is regenerated
solution.why_others_wrong: A, B and C accept the Assertion, which is contradicted by the catalytic cycle described in R.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: nature of enzyme action
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A protein is made of two identical polypeptide chains. Each chain is folded into its own three-dimensional shape, and the two folded chains are arranged with respect to each other in a definite manner. Which of the following statements about this protein are correct?

(a) It shows a quaternary structure.
(b) It has two N-terminal amino acids, one on each chain.
(c) Its primary structure is the sequence of amino acids in its chains.
(d) It is a homopolymer, because its two chains are identical.
(e) Its helical portions are left-handed helices.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: a protein's left end is the first amino acid (N-terminal) and its right end the last (C-terminal), so each polypeptide chain has its own N-terminal amino acid. The primary structure is the sequence of amino acids. When individually folded polypeptides (subunits) are arranged with respect to each other, the protein has a quaternary structure. Each chain is still made of different kinds of amino acids, so the protein is a heteropolymer – identical chains do not make it a homopolymer. In proteins, only right-handed helices are observed.
solution.why_others_wrong: A adds left-handed helices; C and D add the homopolymer claim and leave out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', proteins: structure of proteins
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A human enzyme that has been heated to 70 °C does not regain its activity when it is cooled back to 37 °C.
Reason (R): High temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Effect of high temperature on enzymes
solution.explanation: NCERT: enzymes of most organisms get damaged at high temperatures (say above 40 °C). Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state, whereas high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat. Denaturation destroys the enzyme's structure, so cooling does not bring the activity back – unlike the reversible effect of cold.
steps: Heat denatures the protein → activity destroyed, not just paused → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because denaturation by heat is the very reason activity is not regained; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: factors affecting enzyme activity
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A nucleic acid sample, on complete hydrolysis, gives deoxyribose, phosphoric acid and the bases adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The sample is DNA.
(b) It contains two kinds of substituted purines.
(c) Thymine is a substituted pyrimidine.
(d) The sample is RNA, because it contains adenine and guanine.
(e) The sugar obtained is a hexose.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: a nucleic acid containing deoxyribose is called DNA, while one containing ribose is RNA. Adenine and guanine are substituted purines; uracil, cytosine and thymine are substituted pyrimidines. The sugar in polynucleotides is either ribose or 2′-deoxyribose, both pentoses.
steps: (d) false – the sugar, not the purines, decides DNA versus RNA
solution.why_others_wrong: A leaves out (c); C includes (d) and leaves out (a); D includes (e) and leaves out (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', nucleic acids
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Every enzyme is a protein.
Statement II: Some nucleic acids that behave like enzymes are called ribozymes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: almost all enzymes are proteins. There are some nucleic acids that behave like enzymes; these are called ribozymes. Because of ribozymes, the absolute claim 'every enzyme is a protein' is false.
steps: Statement I → false ('almost all', not every)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and C accept the absolute Statement I, which the existence of ribozymes contradicts; B rejects NCERT's statement about ribozymes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (biomolecule) with List-II (building blocks).

List-I:
A. Inulin
B. Insulin
C. Chitin
D. Cellulose

List-II:
I. Glucose
II. Fructose
III. Amino acids
IV. Amino-sugars and chemically modified sugars

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: inulin is a polymer of fructose; insulin is a protein (a hormone), i.e. a polymer of amino acids; complex polysaccharides such as chitin of the arthropod exoskeleton have amino-sugars and chemically modified sugars (e.g. glucosamine, N-acetyl galactosamine) as building blocks; cellulose is a homopolymer of glucose.
solution.why_others_wrong: B swaps inulin and cellulose; C confuses inulin with insulin; D swaps insulin and chitin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', polysaccharides; proteins
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following enzymes are placed in the correct NCERT class?

(a) An enzyme that hydrolyses the ester bonds of a fat – Hydrolase
(b) An enzyme that transfers an amino group (not hydrogen) from one substrate to another – Transferase
(c) An enzyme that removes a water molecule from a substrate, leaving a double bond – Ligase
(d) An enzyme that converts an optical isomer of a compound into its mirror-image form – Isomerase
(e) An enzyme that moves hydrogen from one substrate to another, oxidising the first – Transferase

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: hydrolases hydrolyse ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic and other bonds; transferases transfer a group G other than hydrogen between two substrates; lyases remove groups by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds; isomerases inter-convert optical, geometric or positional isomers; oxido-reduction between two substrates (including transfer of hydrogen) is catalysed by oxidoreductases/dehydrogenases.
solution.why_others_wrong: A includes (c), which is a lyase reaction; C and D include (e), a redox (hydrogen-transfer) reaction that is not a transferase reaction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: classification and nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Spirometry of a healthy adult gives a total lung capacity of 6000 mL and a functional residual capacity of 2400 mL. What is his inspiratory capacity?

solution.concept: Inspiratory capacity from TLC and FRC
solution.explanation: NCERT: inspiratory capacity (IC) = TV + IRV; functional residual capacity (FRC) = ERV + RV; total lung capacity (TLC) = RV + ERV + TV + IRV. Hence TLC = IC + FRC, and IC = 6000 − 2400 = 3600 mL.
solution.shortcut: Lung capacity splits at the end of a normal expiration: below it is FRC, above it is IC.
solution.why_others_wrong: 8400 mL adds FRC to TLC; 2400 mL is the FRC itself; 4800 mL subtracts a residual volume of 1200 mL from TLC, which gives the vital capacity, not the inspiratory capacity.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', respiratory volumes and capacities
solution.final_answer: Option B: 3600 mL

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: NCERT lists the steps of respiration in order. Which step comes LAST in this list?

options.text: Diffusion of gases across the alveolar membrane
Utilisation of O₂ by the cells for catabolic reactions and the resultant release of CO₂
Transport of gases by the blood

solution.explanation: NCERT: respiration involves (i) breathing or pulmonary ventilation; (ii) diffusion of gases (O₂ and CO₂) across the alveolar membrane; (iii) transport of gases by the blood; (iv) diffusion of O₂ and CO₂ between blood and tissues; and (v) utilisation of O₂ by the cells for catabolic reactions and resultant release of CO₂ (cellular respiration).
solution.why_others_wrong: Breathing is step (i), diffusion across the alveolar membrane step (ii) and transport by blood step (iii).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', mechanism of breathing (steps of respiration)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Utilisation of O₂ by the cells for catabolic reactions and the resultant release of CO₂

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, on an average a healthy human breathes about how many times per minute?

solution.explanation: NCERT: on an average, a healthy human breathes 12–16 times per minute. (70–75 per minute is the rate of action potentials generated by the SA node, i.e. the heart rate range.)
solution.why_others_wrong: 30–40 per minute is far above the NCERT figure; 70–75 per minute is the SA-node (heart) rate; 4–6 per minute is far too low.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', mechanism of breathing
solution.final_answer: Option A: 12–16 times

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A healthy man can inspire or expire approximately 6000 to 8000 mL of air per minute.
Statement II: The vital capacity includes the residual volume.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: tidal volume is approximately 500 mL, i.e. a healthy man can inspire or expire approximately 6000 to 8000 mL of air per minute. Vital capacity is ERV + TV + IRV, the maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration; the residual volume, which remains even after a forcible expiration, is not part of it.
steps: Statement II → false (VC = ERV + TV + IRV)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept that the vital capacity includes the residual volume; B rejects NCERT's figure of 6000–8000 mL per minute.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', respiratory volumes and capacities
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Each haemoglobin molecule can carry a maximum of four molecules of O₂. In a sample, 600 haemoglobin molecules are fully saturated with O₂ and another 400 are exactly half saturated. How many O₂ molecules are bound in all?

solution.explanation: NCERT: each haemoglobin molecule can carry a maximum of four molecules of O₂. Fully saturated molecules carry 4 each and half-saturated molecules carry 2 each: 600 × 4 + 400 × 2 = 2400 + 800 = 3200.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4000 treats all 1000 molecules as fully saturated; 2400 counts only the fully saturated molecules; 1600 takes the maximum load as two O₂ per haemoglobin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', transport of oxygen
solution.final_answer: Option B: 3200

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When the diaphragm and the external inter-costal muscles contract, air flows into the lungs.
Reason (R): Their contraction increases the thoracic volume and hence the pulmonary volume, which decreases the intra-pulmonary pressure to less than the atmospheric pressure.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: contraction of the diaphragm increases the volume of the thoracic chamber in the antero-posterior axis, and contraction of the external inter-costal muscles lifts the ribs and sternum, increasing it in the dorso-ventral axis. The overall increase in thoracic volume causes a similar increase in pulmonary volume, which decreases the intra-pulmonary pressure to less than the atmospheric pressure; this forces air from outside into the lungs.
steps: Volume ↑ → pressure falls below atmospheric → air enters → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because the pressure gradient created by the volume increase is what drives air into the lungs; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', mechanism of breathing
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (respiratory gas and its form of transport) with List-II (approximate per cent carried that way).

List-I:
A. O₂ bound to haemoglobin in RBCs
B. O₂ dissolved in plasma
C. CO₂ as bicarbonate
D. CO₂ dissolved in plasma

List-II:
I. 7
II. 70
III. 3
IV. 97

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: about 97 per cent of O₂ is transported by RBCs in the blood; the remaining 3 per cent is carried in a dissolved state through the plasma. Nearly 20–25 per cent of CO₂ is transported by RBCs (as carbamino-haemoglobin), about 70 per cent is carried as bicarbonate and about 7 per cent in a dissolved state through plasma.
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps the two dissolved fractions; B swaps the haemoglobin-bound O₂ and the bicarbonate; C swaps bicarbonate and dissolved CO₂.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', transport of gases
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: According to the NCERT table of partial pressures, the pO₂ of the tissues equals the pO₂ of deoxygenated blood.
Statement II: According to the same table, the pCO₂ of the tissues equals the pCO₂ of deoxygenated blood.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT table (mm Hg): pO₂ – atmospheric air 159, alveoli 104, deoxygenated blood 40, oxygenated blood 95, tissues 40; pCO₂ – atmospheric air 0.3, alveoli 40, deoxygenated blood 45, oxygenated blood 40, tissues 45. Blood leaving the tissues has come to the same partial pressures as the tissues: pO₂ 40 and pCO₂ 45.
steps: Tissues pO₂ 40 = deoxygenated blood pO₂ 40 → I true
Tissues pCO₂ 45 = deoxygenated blood pCO₂ 45 → II true
solution.why_others_wrong: Both equalities are read directly from the NCERT table, so B, C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', exchange of gases
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (event) with List-II (effect).

List-I:
A. Contraction of the diaphragm
B. Contraction of the external inter-costal muscles
C. Relaxation of the diaphragm and the inter-costal muscles
D. Contraction of additional muscles in the abdomen

List-II:
I. Increases the strength of inspiration and expiration
II. Thoracic and pulmonary volumes decrease and air is expelled
III. Ribs and sternum are lifted, increasing the volume in the dorso-ventral axis
IV. Volume of the thoracic chamber increases in the antero-posterior axis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: contraction of the diaphragm increases the volume of the thoracic chamber in the antero-posterior axis; contraction of the external inter-costal muscles lifts the ribs and sternum, increasing the volume in the dorso-ventral axis; relaxation of the diaphragm and inter-costal muscles reduces the thoracic and pulmonary volumes, leading to expiration; additional muscles in the abdomen can increase the strength of inspiration and expiration.
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps the two axes; C swaps relaxation and the abdominal muscles; D gives the diaphragm the effect of relaxation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', mechanism of breathing
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A healthy adult has a tidal volume of 500 mL, an inspiratory reserve volume of 3000 mL, an expiratory reserve volume of 1000 mL and a residual volume of 1200 mL. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) His inspiratory capacity is 3500 mL.
(b) His vital capacity is 4500 mL.
(c) His functional residual capacity is 2200 mL.
(d) His total lung capacity is 5200 mL.
(e) His expiratory capacity is 1500 mL.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT definitions: IC = TV + IRV = 3500 mL; VC = ERV + TV + IRV = 4500 mL; FRC = ERV + RV = 2200 mL; TLC = RV + ERV + TV + IRV = 5700 mL (not 5200); EC = TV + ERV = 1500 mL.
solution.why_others_wrong: B and C accept a TLC of 5200 mL, which leaves out the expiratory reserve volume; D leaves out the correct vital capacity (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', respiratory volumes and capacities
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: At the alveoli, O₂ diffuses from the alveolar air into the blood while CO₂ diffuses from the blood into the alveolar air, each gas moving from a higher to a lower partial pressure.
Statement II: At the tissues, as at the alveoli, CO₂ diffuses out of the blood.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: pO₂ is 104 mm Hg in the alveoli and 40 in deoxygenated blood, while pCO₂ is 45 in deoxygenated blood and 40 in the alveoli, so at the alveoli O₂ enters and CO₂ leaves the blood. At the tissues the pCO₂ is 45 mm Hg and that of oxygenated blood 40, so CO₂ diffuses from the tissues into the blood – the opposite direction to that at the alveoli.
steps: Statement II → false (at the tissues CO₂ enters the blood)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept Statement II, which reverses the direction of CO₂ movement at the tissues; B rejects Statement I, which follows directly from the NCERT partial pressures.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', exchange of gases
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following respiratory capacities includes the residual volume?

solution.explanation: NCERT: vital capacity = ERV + TV + IRV; inspiratory capacity = TV + IRV; expiratory capacity = TV + ERV; functional residual capacity = ERV + RV. Of these, only the functional residual capacity (and, besides these, the total lung capacity) includes the residual volume.
solution.why_others_wrong: Vital, inspiratory and expiratory capacities are all made of air that can be moved in breathing; none of them contains the residual volume.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', respiratory volumes and capacities
solution.final_answer: Option B: Functional residual capacity

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a person with emphysema, the exchange of gases in the lungs becomes less efficient.
Reason (R): In emphysema, the alveolar walls are damaged, due to which the respiratory surface is decreased.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: emphysema is a chronic disorder in which alveolar walls are damaged, due to which the respiratory surface is decreased; cigarette smoking is one of its major causes. Since the alveoli are the primary sites of exchange of gases, a smaller respiratory surface means less gas exchange, so R explains A.
steps: Damaged alveolar walls → less respiratory surface → less exchange → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because the reduced respiratory surface is the cause of the poorer exchange; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', disorders of respiratory system
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the red blood cells (erythrocytes) of most mammals are:

options.text: Biconcave and devoid of a nucleus

solution.explanation: NCERT: erythrocytes are the most abundant of all the cells in blood. They are formed in the red bone marrow in adults, are devoid of a nucleus in most of the mammals and are biconcave in shape.
steps: Most mammals → RBCs biconcave, without a nucleus
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B describe nucleated RBCs, not those of most mammals; D is not a shape NCERT describes for RBCs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', formed elements: erythrocytes
solution.final_answer: Option C: Biconcave and devoid of a nucleus

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the human heart, the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle is guarded by the:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by a valve formed of three muscular flaps or cusps, the tricuspid valve, whereas a bicuspid or mitral valve guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle. The openings of the right and left ventricles into the pulmonary artery and the aorta are provided with semilunar valves.
solution.why_others_wrong: The tricuspid valve is on the right side; semilunar valves guard the exits into the pulmonary artery and aorta; the inter-atrial septum is a wall between the atria, not a valve.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', human circulatory system: heart
solution.final_answer: Option D: Bicuspid (mitral) valve

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which leucocytes, besides secreting histamine, serotonin and heparin, are described by NCERT as being involved in inflammatory reactions?

solution.explanation: NCERT: basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, heparin, etc., and are involved in inflammatory reactions. Neutrophils and monocytes are phagocytic cells, and lymphocytes (B and T forms) are responsible for immune responses.
steps: Histamine, serotonin, heparin + inflammatory reactions → basophils
solution.why_others_wrong: Neutrophils and monocytes are described as phagocytes; lymphocytes are responsible for immune responses of the body.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', formed elements: leucocytes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Basophils

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Erythrocytes are the most abundant of all the cells in blood.
Statement II: Leucocytes are generally short-lived.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: erythrocytes are the most abundant of all the cells in blood (5 to 5.5 million per mm³ in a healthy adult man). Leucocytes are colourless due to the lack of haemoglobin, are nucleated, relatively lesser in number (6000–8000 per mm³) and generally short-lived.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT's own description, so B, C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', formed elements
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (ABO blood group) with List-II (antigens on the RBCs).

List-I:
A. A
B. B
C. AB
D. O

List-II:
I. Neither A nor B
II. Both A and B
III. B only
IV. A only

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: ABO grouping is based on the presence or absence of two surface antigens, A and B, on the RBCs. Group A has antigen A, group B antigen B, group AB both A and B, and group O neither (nil).
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps groups A and B; B swaps AB and O; D swaps groups A and AB.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', blood groups: ABO grouping
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a person, each ventricle pumps out 70 mL of blood in every cardiac cycle and the heart beats 72 times per minute. What total volume of blood do the two ventricles together pump out in one minute?

solution.explanation: NCERT: during a cardiac cycle each ventricle pumps out approximately 70 mL of blood (the stroke volume). The stroke volume multiplied by the heart rate gives the cardiac output, the volume of blood pumped out by EACH ventricle per minute: 70 × 72 = 5040 mL. Both ventricles together pump 2 × 5040 = 10080 mL per minute (one stream to the lungs, one to the body).
solution.shortcut: Cardiac output is defined per ventricle; double it for the whole heart.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5040 mL is the cardiac output of one ventricle; 2520 mL halves instead of doubling; 140 mL is the output of the two ventricles in a single beat.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', cardiac cycle
solution.final_answer: Option D: 10080 mL

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During ventricular systole, blood is not pushed back from the right ventricle into the right atrium.
Reason (R): The tricuspid valve guarding the opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle allows the flow of blood only in one direction, and it is closed by the attempted backflow.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the valves in the heart allow the flow of blood only in one direction, i.e. from the atria to the ventricles and from the ventricles to the pulmonary artery or aorta, and prevent backward flow. As the ventricles contract, the rising ventricular pressure closes the tricuspid and bicuspid valves due to the attempted backflow of blood into the atria. So the closed tricuspid valve is why blood does not return to the right atrium.
steps: Closed one-way tricuspid valve → no backflow → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because the one-way tricuspid valve is the direct cause of the Assertion; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', human heart; cardiac cycle
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: During joint diastole, blood from the pulmonary veins and the vena cava flows through the atria into the ventricles, because the tricuspid and bicuspid valves are open.
Statement II: The simultaneous contraction of the atria increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by about 30 per cent.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in joint diastole, all four chambers are relaxed; as the tricuspid and bicuspid valves are open, blood from the pulmonary veins and vena cava flows into the left and right ventricles respectively through the left and right atria. The SAN then stimulates both atria to contract simultaneously (atrial systole), which increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by about 30 per cent.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both are NCERT statements; most ventricular filling happens in joint diastole and atrial systole adds about 30 per cent, so B, C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', cardiac cycle
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the human heart are correct?

(a) It has two relatively small upper chambers, the atria, and two larger lower chambers, the ventricles.
(b) The right and left atria are separated by a thin, muscular inter-atrial septum.
(c) The atrium and the ventricle of the same side are separated by a thick fibrous atrio-ventricular septum.
(d) The bicuspid valve guards the opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle.
(e) The sino-atrial node lies in the left atrium.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Chambers and septa of the heart
solution.explanation: NCERT: the heart has four chambers – two relatively small upper chambers called atria and two larger lower chambers called ventricles. A thin, muscular wall called the inter-atrial septum separates the right and left atria, whereas a thick-walled inter-ventricular septum separates the ventricles. The atrium and the ventricle of the same side are separated by a thick fibrous tissue, the atrio-ventricular septum. The tricuspid valve guards the right atrio-ventricular opening, and the SAN lies in the right upper corner of the right atrium.
solution.why_others_wrong: A includes (d); B includes (e) and leaves out (a); D includes (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', human circulatory system: heart
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A heart attack is the condition in which the heart muscle is suddenly damaged by an inadequate blood supply.
Reason (R): A heart attack and cardiac arrest are the same condition, in which the heart stops beating.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: cardiac arrest is when the heart stops beating, whereas a heart attack is when the heart muscle is suddenly damaged by an inadequate blood supply. The two are different, so the Reason is false.
steps: R false – cardiac arrest is a different condition
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B accept the false Reason; D rejects NCERT's definition of a heart attack.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', disorders of circulatory system
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During a sudden fright, the heart beats faster and more forcefully.
Reason (R): Neural signals through the sympathetic nerves can increase the rate of heart beat and the strength of ventricular contraction, and adrenal medullary hormones can also increase the cardiac output.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Neural and hormonal regulation of the heart
solution.explanation: NCERT: neural signals through the sympathetic nerves (part of the ANS) can increase the rate of heart beat, the strength of ventricular contraction and thereby the cardiac output; adrenal medullary hormones can also increase the cardiac output. In an emergency such as fright, the sympathetic system and the adrenal medullary hormones (the emergency hormones) are activated, which is why the heart beats faster and more strongly.
steps: Sympathetic + adrenal medulla → rate and strength ↑ → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B is wrong because the sympathetic and adrenal medullary effects are what produce the faster, stronger beat; C and D are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', regulation of cardiac activity; Class 11 Biology, 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (component) with List-II (approximate share given in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Plasma, as a share of blood
B. Water, as a share of plasma
C. Proteins, as a share of plasma
D. Neutrophils, as a share of total leucocytes

List-II:
I. 60–65 per cent
II. 6–8 per cent
III. 90–92 per cent
IV. About 55 per cent

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: plasma is a straw-coloured, viscous fluid constituting nearly 55 per cent of the blood; 90–92 per cent of plasma is water and proteins contribute 6–8 per cent of it. Neutrophils are the most abundant leucocytes, 60–65 per cent of the total WBCs.
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps plasma and neutrophils; C swaps water and proteins; D swaps plasma and water.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', blood: plasma; formed elements
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
An adult man's blood report shows: RBCs 3.5 million per mm³, haemoglobin 9 g per 100 mL, WBCs 7000 per mm³ and platelets 2,00,000 per mm³. Comparing with the normal values given in NCERT, which of the following statements are correct?

(a) His RBC count is below the normal value.
(b) His haemoglobin is below the normal range.
(c) His WBC count is within the normal range.
(d) His platelet count is below normal, so he is likely to have clotting disorders.
(e) His low haemoglobin can reduce the transport of respiratory gases by his blood.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT normal values: RBCs 5 to 5.5 million per mm³ (healthy adult man); haemoglobin 12–16 g per 100 mL; WBCs 6000–8000 per mm³; platelets 1,50,000–3,50,000 per mm³. Haemoglobin molecules play a significant role in the transport of respiratory gases. So 3.5 million RBCs and 9 g haemoglobin are low, 7000 WBCs is normal, and 2,00,000 platelets is within the normal range.
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B include (d), though the platelet count is normal; C leaves out the true statement (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', blood: formed elements
